public_rationale: Mistral had released a model for independent use before the post, and the BLOOM research report documents a substantial development community. These records support Marcus’s technical point that usable LLMs and relevant knowledge were already distributed beyond OpenAI. They do not prove that OpenAI made the alleged threat or that copyright restrictions could have no effect on those models.
limitations: The result uses the ordinary public-model reading of open source.
Project contributors had different roles; their number is not a count of people able to train a complete model alone.
Technical availability does not establish legal immunity, affordability, or indefinite persistence.

our_interpretation: The ordinary technical reading is that independently usable LLM releases and substantial development expertise already existed outside OpenAI.
Open source is read here as publicly downloadable models with permission for independent use, rather than a guarantee that every training input is available.
A large number means a substantial development community, without inventing a numerical threshold.
The word already describes accumulated releases and expertise before the post, so the target period has no specified beginning and ends on 2024-01-08.

The empty-threat inference concerns technical dependence on individual suppliers. It does not establish that OpenAI actually made the attributed threat or that every model was legally immune from copyright claims.
